data.question: Does the river width SWOT reports for the Baton Rouge reach tell me anything about stage? width_m for reach 74210000331 Version D against the stage at USGS-07374000; does a leveed reach widen at all; bad passes

data.takes: SIGNED. Warns: name the level. Everything here is the reach level width, a product aggregate over roughly 10 km, set beside a point stage.

SIGNED. Rules in: name the collection (SWOT_L2_HR_RiverSP_reach_D), pair each pass with a gauge reading inside 15 minutes and drop unpaired passes by name, score changes between consecutive pairs with capped lag-1 sampling intervals, refuse fewer than ten pairs. Written for height; says nothing about width. Width has no datum problem, so levels of width may be set beside stage, but I keep change scores as well so they can be read beside the height worked example (change correlation +0.957). Warns: gauge provisional throughout 2024.

SIGNED. Rules in: reach level width with its own width_u exists in the granule; quality attributes are categorical gates, not uncertainty. Rules out: calling a comparison with discharge a confrontation. Missing for this question: what the reach width is (how it is aggregated, whether dark water is filled from a prior, how it is bounded) is not stated.

SIGNED. Rules in: Version D only, named. Rules out: mixing in the Version C block. Warns: Version D height range at this reach in 2024 is -0.534 to 10.201 m; the gauge put the 2024 surface between 1.47 and 10.37 m with datum at zero.
SIGNED. Warns: fill values are large negatives and must be filtered, not averaged; check width_m for fills before any statistic. Says width is served; gives no definition of it.

NOT SIGNED (in the wiki, status draft). Warns that levels of height across datums are uninterpretable; does not bind width, a length across the river with no vertical reference. Used only to say why width levels may be read where height levels may not.

SIGNED, about lakes. By analogy only: for lakes dark_frac is one minus the detected fraction and dark water area is filled from a prior water probability map. If reach width is built the same way, a high dark_frac pass would report a width partly from a prior; no page says this for rivers, so it is a thing to look at, not a fact. Rules out carrying the lake quality ladder over to reach_q.
Its signature line names a person while its status reads draft. About lake identifiers; changes nothing for a fixed SWORD reach.
SIGNED. About lake height datums; changes nothing for width.
SIGNED. Another gauge confrontation, for modelled flow; shares the form of the scores only. Changes nothing here.
SIGNED. Annual peaks; listed on the word width (a fixed-width file). Changes nothing here.
SIGNED. Stage is parameter 00065, gage height. Changes nothing else here.
SIGNED. About the peaks collection; changes nothing here.
SIGNED. About flood frequency fits; changes nothing here.
SIGNED; not in the list, read because the recipe points at approval status. Warns: the gauge side is provisional throughout 2024 and may be revised; say so beside any number.

DRAFT in the queue, not signed. Saves a look at the file's shape: 52 Version D passes with time, wse_m, wse_u_m, width_m, slope, reach_q, dark_frac, ice_clim_f, and 386 gauge readings kept within 60 minutes of each pass; so no width_u, no CRID, no pass number, and the passes of 2024-02-23 and 2024-03-15 do not pair at 15 minutes. To be checked on my own data before relying on it. Warns that stage is known only at passes.

DRAFT in the queue, not signed. Names two passes whose height departs from the gauge: 2024-10-30 (1.776 m low) and 2024-03-26 (0.947 m high). This is the scientist's stated worry (bad passes may have bad widths), so I look at the width on those two dates by name instead of rediscovering them, and report any width score with and without them. Warns: a pass enters two changes; list every pass before reading a summary. The draft offers no screen and I write none.

DRAFT in the queue, not signed. Says reach slope rises with stage here and the gauge to reach distance is undefined. For width it warns only that a reach aggregate is not the cross section at the gauge; no slope correction applies to width.

DRAFT in the queue, not signed. Saves the flag census: reach_q 1 on 49 passes, 2 on 3, never 0; meaning of the values cited nowhere. Rules out describing passes as good or flagged from reach_q and rules out my writing a screen from it. I may split by it as description only.

data.about: SWOT RiverSP reach width (width_m) in datasets/swot-river-lake.md and connectors/hydrocron-swot.md
data.text: Seen while exploring, one reach, one year. The reported reach width differs by overpass track at like stage. The 52 Version D passes of 2024 at reach 74210000331 fall on three tracks (17, 18 and 17 passes). In all 17 pairs of passes one or two days apart, with the stage moving by at most 0.652 m inside a pair, the second track reports a narrower river than the first: mean difference -39.3 m, median -31.7 m. That offset is about as large as the whole rise of width over the year's stage range on any one track (slope about 7 m of width per metre of stage over about 9 m). Among passes with dark_frac below 0.05 the two track lines still differ by 29.5 m at 5 m stage, so dark water alone does not look like the cause. The signed pages list width and width_u and say nothing of what the reach width is, how it is bounded, or that it may depend on viewing geometry; the cause is not known from this file. Who could say: the RiverSP product description, which no page cites, or PO.DAAC. Until then a width series that mixes tracks should not be read as the river.

data.about: the fixture swot_gauge_baton_rouge_2024.json and what marks an unusable width
data.text: Seen while exploring. The pass of 2024-02-12 reports a width of 937.3 m, 89.0 m above its own track's line on stage and 116.5 m wider than the pass of the next day at a stage 0.122 m higher, while its height agrees with the gauge (departure +0.083 m from the median difference). Nothing the file keeps marks it: dark_frac 0.015, reach_q 1, stated height uncertainty 0.094 m. The file has no width_u, which the signed river and lake page says the granule carries; whether width_u is large on that pass cannot be seen. The other way round, the pass of 2024-03-26 (dark_frac 0.692, height +0.947 m off) has a width 29.9 m below its track's line. So in this year a wrong width and a wrong height came together once and apart twice (2024-02-12 width only, 2024-10-30 height only). Three passes fix no rate. Asking the fetch script to keep width_u, cycle and pass number would let the next reader see more; the drafted fixture page in the queue (not signed) already asks for cycle and pass.

data.about: the SWOT repeat period and overpass track identity, in the knowledge base
data.text: No page read for this question states the repeat period of the science orbit, and the fixture has no pass number (the drafted fixture page, not signed, says so). I first grouped passes with a period supplied from memory, 20.86455 d, which the read-what-is-known skill does not allow as a fact. The file itself shows intervals between passes of one track with median 20.86464 d, and a grouping from the gaps alone agrees with the phase grouping on every pass once the missing pass of 2024-03-25 is allowed for. A page that states the repeat, or a fixture that keeps pass_id, would remove the inference.

data.about: LOOK-008, a scan for the repeat period
data.text: Dead end, kept in the record: the scan scored candidate periods by the fewest phase groups, which rewards merging two tracks 1.45 d apart, and returned 20.9384 d with two groups. The scoring was wrong, not the data. LOOK-010 replaces it.
